newsitem.title: UK: Jersey fund managers optimistic on 1997 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Jersey fund managers optimistic on 1997 - survey.

text.p: Jersey fund managers are optimistic about business prospects for 1997 after a strong 1996 and are investing in staff and technology in the face of increasing competition, a Coopers and Lybrand survey showed.
The Jersey Fund Managers Association said net sales of collective investment funds rose to 3.97 billion stg from 2.53 billion in 1995 and 0.96 billion in 1994.
The survey said the most important sources of new business were UK expatriates, the UK and Middle East, followed by the Far East, EU and Switzerland.

It showed 90 percent of JFMA members were as optimistic or more optimistic on the overall business climate in 1997 than in 1996, with 93 percent expecting to hold or increase the value of their business.
It said 70 percent saw increased volumes in 1996.

"Fund managers recognise that competition is fierce from other jurisdictions and they are taking steps to invest in technology and training to increase efficiency and expand capacity," JFMA chairman Martin Dryden said.
Staff numbers decreased at 17 percent of members in 1996, although 93 percent the proportion of staff costs to total costs had stayed the same or increased.
